title: Navigation Compose: routes, arguments and the back stack

videos.script: One activity, and many screens. Something has to know which screen is showing, and what back should do. {{host}} That something is a NavHost and its controller. The planner gets three screens: the courses, one course, and a form to add a session. Each screen is a route, and each route is a Kotlin type. {{args}} A route can carry arguments. The planner passes an id, and never the object, and this lesson says why. {{stack}} Then the back stack, printed after every tap. Navigate pushes, pop removes, and the screen you see is the one on top. {{popupto}} Then the two ways a stack grows wrong. A double tap pushes the same screen twice. And going back to the list by navigating forward leaves the old screens underneath. {{back}} And last, the system's back gesture, which the NavHost answers for you. Three presses, and the third one closes the app.
